published_figures.source: Cessna Model 172P Pilot's Operating Handbook, 12 May 1981
published_figures.figure: Section 2, powerplant limitations: "The static RPM range at full throttle (carburetor heat off and mixture leaned to maximum RPM) is 2300 to 2420 RPM."
Section 1, engine: the Lycoming O-320-D2J, "160 rated BHP at 2700 RPM"; full throttle and full rich at sea level, the propeller turning 2,700.

Section 1, performance specifications: ground roll 890 ft; figure 5-5 gives it for a short-field take-off - flaps 10, full throttle before brake release, paved level dry runway, zero wind, sea level, 2400 lb - with lift-off at 51 KIAS, which figure 5-1 makes 55.6 KCAS with 10 degrees of flap.

Section 1, performance specifications: rate of climb at sea level 700 FPM; figure 5-6 gives it at 76 KIAS, flaps up, full throttle, 2400 lb, and 700 between its 0 C and 20 C columns at the standard 15 C. 76 KIAS is 75.4 KCAS by figure 5-1.

Section 1, performance specifications: service ceiling 13,000 ft. Figure 5-6, maximum rate of climb, 2400 lb, flaps up, full throttle, "mixture leaned above 3000 feet for maximum RPM": the climb speed falls from 76 KIAS at sea level to 70 at 12,000 ft, 75.4 to 70 KCAS by figure 5-1, so 0.45 kt a thousand feet; the rate at the standard temperature is about 150 ft/min at 12,000 ft, 100 near 13,000. The ceiling is the height at which the best climb has fallen to 100 ft/min. Flown by the autopilot, as the AI climbs, at figure 5-6's speeds, leaning as it goes. The tolerance is this project's, as the climb rate's is.
Figure 5-8, cruise performance: 121 KTAS at 8000 ft, standard temperature, 2650 RPM (77% power), 2400 lb, mixture leaned. Section 1 gives 120 knots at 75% power at 8000 ft.

Figure 3-1, maximum glide: 65 KIAS, propeller windmilling, flaps up, zero wind, drawn as 18 nautical miles from 12,000 ft above the terrain, which is 9.1 to 1. 65 KIAS is 66 KCAS by figure 5-1. The figure is a chart, read by eye; the tolerance allows for that.
Figure 5-3, stall speeds, 2400 lb, power off, wings level, flaps up: 51 KCAS at the most rearward centre of gravity and 52 KCAS at the most forward. The range is 2 kt either side of those.
Figure 5-3, stall speeds, 2400 lb, power off, wings level, flaps 10 degrees: 48 KCAS rearward and 49 KCAS forward centre of gravity, 2 kt either side.
Figure 5-3, stall speeds, 2400 lb, power off, wings level, flaps 30 degrees: 46 KCAS at either centre of gravity, 2 kt either side.
published_figures.plan_speeds: The slowest, 60 kt, is its approach speed, the slowest any plan was ever let fly it: flown clean, it held all four ways round its 521 m circle. The fastest, 110 kt, is 5 kt under the fastest that held with 5 kt of power in hand: she flies level at 124 kt at full throttle at 3,000 ft, so 115 kt is the most a plan may ask that leaves her that (sim::holds_plan_speed, 2026-10-06; it was 120).
published_figures.glide_speeds: 60 kt, the slowest a route may fly it, went round unstalled.
published_figures.landing_distance: Section 1, performance specifications, of the 1985 Model 172P handbook (the printing read for this; the 1981 one above was not to hand): total distance over a 50 ft obstacle 1280 ft - figure 5-11, short field, flaps 30, power off, maximum braking, paved level dry runway, zero wind, 2400 lb, sea level, between its 10 C 1265 ft and 20 C 1295 ft. Times 1.43, a light aeroplane's margin: the landing distance within 70 per cent of the landing distance available, EASA Air OPS CAT.POL.A.330(a) for performance class B, which the UK CAA's Safety Sense leaflet 7, Aeroplane Performance, recommends to every pilot.
